spots.name: Chorsu Bazaar
spots.summary: Chorsu Bazaar, also called Charsu Bazaar, is the traditional bazaar located in the center of the old town of Tashkent, the capital city of Uzbekistan. Under its blue-colored domed building and the adjacent areas, all daily necessities are sold.

spots.name: Amir Timur Museum
spots.summary: The Amir Timur Museum is located in Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan. It opened in 1996, and is dedicated to the Turco-Mongol warlord Amir Timur (Tamerlane).

spots.name: Kukeldash Madrasah
spots.summary: Kukeldash Madrasah is a medieval madrasa in Tashkent, located close to Chorsu Bazaar and Chorsu Metro station. It was built around 1570 by the Uzbek Shaybanid ruler Dervish Sultan.

spots.name: Hazrati Imam Complex
spots.summary: The Hazrati Imam complex is an architectural monument dating from the 16th to 20th centuries, located in the Olmazor district of Tashkent city, Uzbekistan.

spots.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral
spots.summary: The Sacred Heart Cathedral is a religious building belonging to the Roman Catholic Church, located at the street Sadiq Asimov, Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan.

spots.name: State Museum of History of Uzbekistan
spots.summary: The State Museum of History of Uzbekistan, previously known as the National Museum of Turkestan, was founded in 1876. It is located in Tashkent.
spots.wikipediaTitle: State Museum of History of Uzbekistan

spots.name: Navoi Theater
spots.summary: The Navoi Theater, officially the Alisher Navoi State Academic Grand Theatre, is a national opera theater in central Tashkent, built as one of the first modern theaters in the region.

spots.name: Holy Assumption Cathedral Church
spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Assumption of the Virgin or more properly the Cathedral of the Dormition of the Mother of God is the Russian Orthodox cathedral of the diocese of Tashkent in Uzbekistan since 1945. The cathedral was built in 1871 and enlarged in the 1990s, the bell tower was rebuilt in 2010.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of the Assumption of the Virgin, Tashkent

spots.name: Romanov Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Romanov Palace, located in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, was built in 1891 according to the design of architect V.S Geintselman and A.L. Benois for Grand Duke Nikolai Konstantinovich, who had been exiled to the outskirts of the empire in the Turkestan region.

spots.name: State Museum of Applied Arts of Uzbekistan
spots.summary: The State Museum of Applied Arts of Uzbekistan is an art museum located in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, founded in 1937 as a temporary exhibition for handicrafts.
spots.wikipediaTitle: State Museum of Applied Arts of Uzbekistan

spots.name: Museum of Arts of Uzbekistan
spots.summary: The Museum of Arts of Uzbekistan is the largest national art museum in Tashkent, Republic of Uzbekistan. Its permanent collection contains more than several thousands works, divided among four curatorial departments.

spots.name: Qaffol Shoshi mausoleum
spots.summary: Qaffol Shoshi mausoleum is a mausoleum in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, built in honor of Imam Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ismail al-Kaffal ash-Shashi. The original tomb did not survive in its initial form. In its current state, the mausoleum was constructed in 1542 by the royal architect of that time, Gulyam Husayn.

spots.name: Amir Timur Square
spots.summary: The Amir Timur Square is the main town square in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

spots.name: Art Gallery of Uzbekistan
spots.summary: The Art Gallery of Uzbekistan is a museum in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Established after independence in 1991, it is one of the most visited modern museums in Uzbekistan.

spots.name: Museum of Victims of Political Repression in Tashkent
spots.summary: The Museum of Victims of Political Repression in Tashkent is a museum which tells the history of Uzbekistan during the political repression in the Soviet Union, in particular that of the people killed at that time.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Victims of Political Repression in Tashkent

spots.name: Sheihantaur complex
spots.summary: The Sheikh Hovendi at-Tahur Complex is an architectural complex, centered around the Mausoleum of Sheikh Hovendi at-Tahur (Sheikhantaur). It is one of the most important architectural monuments of Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

spots.name: Dzhuma Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Khoja Ahror Valiy mosque is a mosque in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Also known as the Jama or Dzhuma Mosque, it was built in 1451 by Sheikh Ubaydullo Khoja Akhror (1404–1490).

spots.name: Tashkent City Park
spots.summary: Tashkent City Park is a city park in the center of Tashkent, the largest recreational park area in Uzbekistan. Located on the territory of the international business center Tashkent City.

spots.name: Memory and Honor Square
spots.summary: The Memory and Honor Square is a war memorial complex in Tashkent dedicated to the memory of Soviet soldiers who died in the World War II. It is located on Mustaqillik Maydoni in Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan. The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is located on the territory of this memorial complex.

spots.name: Sheihantaur
spots.summary: Sheihantaur is a historic mausoleum complex in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. It is the burial site of Sheikh Hovendi at-Tahur, a local Sufi figure of historical significance.

spots.name: State Museum of Nature of Uzbekistan

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Uzbekistan State Museum of Nature is one of the oldest museums in Uzbekistan. The museum's main purpose is to show the natural beauty of Uzbekistan and to help protect its environment. The museum features chronologically-ordered exhibits and seeks to educate visitors about Uzbekistan's geography through time.
spots.wikipediaTitle: State Museum of Nature of Uzbekistan

spots.name: Abulkasym Madrassah
spots.summary: The Abulkasym Madrassah is an architectural monument located in Tashkent, Tashkent Province, Uzbekistan. It consists of a madrasa, a mosque and a khanaqah. The building was the location of the signing of a peace treaty in 1865 following the Russian capture of Tashkent.

spots.name: Tashkent Museum of Railway Techniques
spots.summary: Tashkent Museum of Railway Equipment is a railway museum in Tashkent and is the only such museum in Uzbekistan.

spots.name: Milliy Stadium
spots.summary: The Milliy Stadium, formerly known as the Bunyodkor Stadium, is a football stadium in the city of Tashkent — the capital of Uzbekistan. Located in Chilanzar District of Tashkent, on Bunyodkor Avenue. It seats 34,000 spectators, thus becoming the largest stadium in Uzbekistan.

spots.name: The Alisher Navoi State Museum of Literature

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Alisher Navoi State Museum of Literature of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan is a scientific-cultural, educational establishment which mainly focuses on collecting and researching the historical materials and objects which are related to Uzbekistan's history.
spots.wikipediaTitle: The Alisher Navoi State Museum of Literature

spots.name: The Museum of Communication History in Uzbekistan
spots.summary: The Museum of Communication History in Uzbekistan, is a unique and the first museum in the history of Uzbekistan which is related to the communication technologies. It was established in 2009, and nowadays the museum became one of the most famous museums among Uzbek people.
spots.wikipediaTitle: The Museum of Communication History in Uzbekistan

spots.name: Tashkent botanical garden
spots.summary: Tranquil wooded garden over 66 hectares, the autumn colours are glorious.

spots.name: Martyrs' Memorial
spots.summary: The Martyrs' Memorial, is a monument located along the Bozsu Canal, in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Built near the "Devil's bridge", it was one of the main places for executions and graves for victims of the Great Purge in the USSR. Museum of Victims of Political Repression stands next to the monument.

spots.summary: Built in 1899 to serve the city's German community. Under the communists it was variously a warehouse, opera studio and concert hall, then re-consecrated in the 1990s. It is not open to the public except for attending services.
